findings.evidence: Diff removes `[Fact p.Prime]` at SplitsCompletely.lean:89; the proof (lines 92-110) uses only `Algebra.IsInvariant.orbit_eq_primesOver` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Invariant/Basic.lean:166, no primality hypothesis), orbit-stabilizer, and `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`. `scripts/lint-baseline.txt:64` reads `unusedArguments TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot`, i.e. the linter had flagged exactly this argument under the old name; scripts/ is human-owned so the entry could not be renamed.
findings.fix: Either restore `[Fact p.Prime]` (and let a human rename the baseline entry), or keep the generalization and say so: state it in the PR description and amend the docstring to note that primality is not required (it is forced by `Q.IsPrime` + `Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})`). Either way `scripts/lint-baseline.txt:64` still names the pre-move declaration and needs a human update.
findings.issue: The migration silently drops `[Fact p.Prime]` from the public statement of `ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot`, which the PR describes as a pure namespace move. The statement is now about an arbitrary `p : ℕ` while its docstring (line 85) still says "a prime `Q` of `𝓞 L` above the rational prime `p`". The change is true but is a scope widening made to dodge a lint entry, not part of the move.

summary: The rename itself is faithful: every retargeted reference resolves to the same declaration and no statement is captured by a Mathlib homonym. One non-mechanical change is bundled in undisclosed — `ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot` silently lost its `[Fact p.Prime]` hypothesis while its docstring still describes a rational prime.
